title: Postgram
summary: Virtual postcards pinned to a physical place. The sender leaves them from a specific spot; the recipient can only open them by being there. A social network that makes you move.
problem: Social feeds live on the phone and in the instant: open, scroll, close. Postgram starts from the opposite idea — the message only unlocks if you go to the place where it was left.
audience: Friends and people close to me. Starting with myself.
responsibilities: Full flow to create a postcard: photo, message and location.
Proximity unlock: the recipient only sees the content when they're on the spot.
Onboarding that explains the mechanic without fuss.
decisions: Location isn't metadata — it's the condition for seeing the message.
Deliberately simple app. If it adds physical friction, that friction is the product.
Rails to ship the full cycle without inventing extra infrastructure.
outcomes: A working prototype with the create, receive and open cycle.
Proof that mixing social and the physical world can work without a complicated interface.
